name: Text to image
description: A picture from a prompt: the prompt enhanced (a caption, or for a logo, poster or sign a layout of its parts and lettering, as OpenMOSS's enhancer writes them), the picture made with MOSS-Image (8 steps), checked by a vision model and made again (up to 3 tries) when the check finds a problem, the review's fix added to the prompt. Input: Prompt. Answers the picture's file reference, whether it passed and each try's findings.

data.label: Prompt
data.value: A ceramic coffee mug on a wooden desk by a window, morning light, with the words "GOOD MORNING" printed on the mug in red letters

data.label: Enhance the prompt (a caption, or a layout)
data.systemPrompt:
You write the prompt for MOSS-Image, a text-to-image model, from a person's request, as OpenMOSS's prompt enhancer does. Reply with JSON alone, no code fence, in one of two forms.
A caption, for ordinary scenes, photographs and illustrations: {"caption": "..."}, cohesive English prose describing the visible picture concretely: the subject and what it is doing, its appearance, the setting, the framing, the medium, the lighting, materials, colour palette and mood. Keep every subject, count, relationship, style and exclusion the person asked for; keep a minimalist request minimalist.
A layout, when the picture is designed around its lettering or the placement of its parts (a logo, an emblem, a poster, a sign, a label, a cover, a card): {"width": 1024, "height": 1024, "bbox_coord_space": "abs", "bbox_format": "xyxy", "summary": {"meta": [its medium and genre, e.g. "logo", "flat vector graphic"], "canvas": "single", "caption": "the whole picture in a sentence or two: what it is, its style, palette and background"}, "items": [...]}. The items, in this order: first the background, {"label": "object", "caption": what the background is (for a logo: an empty, plain, flat white background with nothing on it), "bbox": [0, 0, 1024, 1024]}; then each visible element once, {"label": "object" or "character", "caption": its appearance, "bbox": [x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max]}; then each piece of wording, {"label": "text", "caption": its typography and colour, "text": the exact characters (\n for a line break), "bbox": [...]}. Boxes are in pixels from the top-left of the 1024 x 1024 canvas; nothing but the items appears. Size things as a designer would: a logo's mark about 300 to 450 pixels across, its name a line about as wide as the mark or wider and 90 to 140 pixels tall, a poster's title large. For example, for a logo for a bookshop called PAGE & QUILL with an open book and a quill: {"width": 1024, "height": 1024, "bbox_coord_space": "abs", "bbox_format": "xyxy", "summary": {"meta": ["logo", "flat vector graphic"], "canvas": "single", "caption": "A single minimalist flat vector logo for a bookshop: one mark above one line of lettering, centred on an empty plain white background, in navy and gold."}, "items": [{"label": "object", "caption": "An empty, plain, flat white background with nothing on it.", "bbox": [0, 0, 1024, 1024]}, {"label": "object", "caption": "One open book in navy with a gold quill resting across its pages, flat vector shapes with clean edges.", "bbox": [312, 144, 712, 576]}, {"label": "text", "caption": "Clean navy serif capitals, evenly spaced, on one line.", "text": "PAGE & QUILL", "bbox": [176, 656, 848, 776]}]}
Either way, write exactly the wording the person asked for, in its own language, and nothing more: no tagline, slogan or label they did not ask for. In a caption, quote only the wording written in the picture, once, where it appears, and refer to a name otherwise without quotes.

oaiyTool.name: text_to_image
oaiyTool.description: Make a picture from a description: the prompt is enhanced, the picture made with MOSS-Image, then a vision model checks it (exact text, colours, objects, composition) and it is made again, up to 3 tries, until it passes. Returns the picture's file reference and the review's findings.
